title: Euler tour
statementMd:
Euler is a little, cute squirrel. When the autumn comes, he collects some reserves for winter. The interesting fact is that Euler likes to collect acorns in a specific way. A tree can be described as 𝑛n acorns connected by 𝑛−1n−1 branches, such that there is exactly one way between each pair of acorns. Let's enumerate the acorns from 11 to 𝑛n.

The squirrel chooses one acorn (not necessary with number 11) as a start, and visits them in a way called "Euler tour" (see notes), collecting each acorn when he visits it for the last time.

Today morning Kate was observing Euler. She took a sheet of paper and wrote down consecutive indices of acorns on his path. Unfortunately, during her way to home it started raining and some of numbers became illegible. Now the girl is very sad, because she has to present the observations to her teacher.

"Maybe if I guess the lacking numbers, I'll be able to do it!" she thought. Help her and restore any valid Euler tour of some tree or tell that she must have made a mistake.

## Input

The first line contains a single integer 𝑛n (1≤𝑛≤5⋅1051≤n≤5⋅105), denoting the number of acorns in the tree.

The second line contains 2𝑛−12n−1 integers 𝑎1,𝑎2,…,𝑎2𝑛−1a1,a2,…,a2n−1 (0≤𝑎𝑖≤𝑛0≤ai≤n) — the Euler tour of the tree that Kate wrote down. 00 means an illegible number, which has to be guessed.

## Output

If there is no Euler tour satisfying the given description, output "`no`" in the first line.

Otherwise, on the first line output "`yes`", and then in the second line print the Euler tour which satisfy the given description.

Any valid Euler tour will be accepted, since the teacher doesn't know how exactly the initial tree looks.

## Note

An Euler tour of a tree with 𝑛n acorns is a sequence of 2𝑛−12n−1 indices of acorns. such that each acorn occurs at least once, the first and the last acorns are same and each two consecutive acorns are directly connected with a branch.
statementZhMd:
Euler 是一只可爱的小松鼠。秋天来临时，他会为冬天收集一些储备。Euler 收集橡果的方式很特别。一棵树可以描述为由 $n$ 个橡果和 $n-1$ 条树枝连接而成的结构，使得任意一对橡果之间恰好存在一条路径。我们将这些橡果编号为 $1$ 到 $n$。

松鼠选择一个橡果作为起点（不一定是编号为 $1$ 的橡果），并按照一种称为“欧拉遍历”的方式访问它们（见说明），每当他最后一次访问某个橡果时，就收集这个橡果。

今天早上，Kate 观察了 Euler。她在纸上写下了他经过的路径中连续的橡果编号。不幸的是，在回家的路上开始下雨，其中一些数字变得无法辨认。现在女孩非常难过，因为她必须向老师展示这次观察结果。

“或许只要猜出缺失的数字，我就能完成这件事！”她想道。请帮助她恢复任意一个满足条件的树的有效欧拉遍历，或者判断她一定弄错了。

## 输入格式

第一行包含一个整数 $n$（$1\le n\le 5\cdot 10^5$），表示树中橡果的数量。

第二行包含 $2n-1$ 个整数 $a_1,a_2,\ldots,a_{2n-1}$（$0\le a_i\le n$）——Kate 记录下来的树的欧拉遍历。$0$ 表示无法辨认的数字，需要将其补全。

## 输出格式

如果不存在满足描述的欧拉遍历，第一行输出 `no`。

否则，第一行输出 `yes`，然后在第二行输出一个满足描述的欧拉遍历。

任何有效的欧拉遍历都会被接受，因为老师并不知道原树的具体结构。

## 说明

一棵有 $n$ 个橡果的树的欧拉遍历是一个长度为 $2n-1$ 的橡果编号序列，满足：每个橡果至少出现一次；第一个和最后一个橡果相同；并且每两个相邻的橡果都通过一条树枝直接相连。
